title: Payment System
oneLine: Drive every payment through an idempotent state machine, record money in an append-only double-entry ledger, treat PSP responses as uncertain evidence, and reconcile settlement independently.
opening: I would separate payment orchestration from accounting. The client creates a payment order with an idempotency key and amount represented as decimal/minor units, never floating point. A durable state machine validates the order, persists it, and calls the PSP with its own idempotency key. Timeouts do not mean failure; PSP webhooks and status polling are ingested idempotently and advance only legal state transitions. Monetary effects are posted to an append-only double-entry ledger where every transaction balances debits and credits; corrections are compensating entries, never edits. A transactional outbox publishes downstream events. Settlement files and bank/PSP reports feed a reconciliation system that compares internal orders, ledger, PSP events, and cash movement, then creates exceptions or adjustments. PCI scope is minimized through hosted payment pages/tokenization, and refunds/chargebacks are separate linked workflows.
ask: Pay-in, payout, refund, chargeback, or which flows?
Card, bank transfer, wallet, and which PSPs/regions/currencies?
What does success mean: authorized, captured, settled, or available?
Availability, latency, consistency, and regulatory/audit requirements?
scale: Payment TPS may be modest compared with feeds, but correctness and long-lived workflows dominate design.
Use integer minor units or fixed decimal with currency-specific scale; never binary floating point.
Retain immutable business, provider, ledger, and reconciliation evidence according to regulation.

decisions.default: Payment order state for workflow; double-entry ledger for money/accounting.
decisions.why: Operational status and financial truth are related but not identical.
decisions.switch: Never derive balances solely from PSP callbacks or a mutable status column.

decisions.default: Idempotent PSP request plus webhook inbox and reconciliation.
decisions.why: Network timeout leaves outcome unknown and retries are unavoidable.
decisions.switch: Provider-specific query/status API resolves ambiguous cases; do not guess.

decisions.why: It makes retries, timeouts, compensation, and operator recovery visible.
decisions.switch: A workflow engine can implement it, but the business states/invariants remain yours.

decisions.default: Append-only balanced postings and compensating entries.
decisions.why: Audit trails and historical balances must remain reproducible.
decisions.switch: Materialized balances are caches/views validated against postings.

deepDives.title: Double-entry ledger
points: Each ledger transaction contains at least two postings whose signed amounts balance per currency.
Use immutable transaction ID, account, amount, currency, effective/booked time, and reference lineage.
Postings and materialized balance update occur atomically; periodically recompute/check balances.

deepDives.title: Idempotency
points: Scope key to merchant/customer operation and persist request fingerprint plus final/in-progress response.
Reject same key with different payload.
Use inbox for webhooks and outbox for emitted events so retries are harmless.

deepDives.title: Reconciliation
points: Match internal order, PSP transaction, settlement batch, fees, refunds, and bank cash.
Classify timing differences versus real discrepancies.
Exceptions are durable cases with owner, evidence, resolution, and append-only adjustment.

deepDives.title: Security
points: Tokenize card data and use hosted fields/pages to reduce PCI scope.
Encrypt secrets, rotate keys, sign/verify webhooks, enforce least privilege and dual control.
Separate fraud/risk decision evidence from payment state.

failures.risk: PSP call times out after charge succeeded
failures.response: Keep UNKNOWN/PENDING, retry with same provider idempotency key, ingest webhook/status, and reconcile—never charge with a new key.

failures.risk: Webhook duplicated or out of order
failures.response: Unique provider event inbox and legal monotonic state transitions; store all evidence.

failures.risk: Ledger posting succeeds but event publish fails
failures.response: Transactional outbox in the same DB commit; publisher retries until acknowledged.
Reconciliation opens an exception, blocks premature finality where necessary, and posts explicit adjustment after investigation.

questions.q: Why do we need a ledger if the PSP has records?
questions.a: The PSP is an external operational counterparty, not your complete accounting source. You need internal fees, liabilities, refunds, merchant balances, timing, and an auditable view independent of provider availability.

questions.q: Can a payment API return success immediately?
questions.a: Only if the defined state is reached. ‘Authorized’ is not ‘captured’ or ‘settled.’ Return a payment resource/status and support asynchronous completion for uncertain or slow rails.

questions.q: How do you ensure exactly-once payment?
questions.a: There is no magic distributed exactly once. Use idempotency at client, orchestration, provider, webhook, ledger, and event boundaries, then reconciliation to detect residual uncertainty.
Create a linked idempotent refund workflow, call the rail/provider, ingest evidence, and append reversing/appropriate ledger postings. Do not mutate the original payment.

mistakes: Saying Kafka gives exactly-once money movement
seniorSignal: Be exact about state meanings and uncertainty. Anchor the answer on invariants, double-entry accounting, idempotency at every boundary, append-only evidence, and operational reconciliation.
implementation: Spring Boot payment state machine with PostgreSQL transactions
Append-only ledger tables plus balanced constraint/materialized balances
PSP adapters with idempotency, signed webhook inbox, and status polling
Transactional outbox/Kafka and a separate reconciliation/exception service
